Scenario: AC5 A settlement offer below the floor is routed to the approver with the gap to the floor and moves to AWAITING_APPROVAL_SET with a three-working-day clock (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC6 A transfer price below the floor is routed for a second signature and moves to AWAITING_SECOND_SIGNATURE with a three-working-day clock (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC7 A refused second signature returns the case to the route decision with reason `price_below_floor`, and a refused settlement approval records the reason and the gap (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC8 A granted approval releases the offer to the customer, or generates the documents for a deed in lieu (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC9 The approval routes to the level the delegation of authority names for the product, the decision and the amount on the routing date, and the level and limit version are written with the answer (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC10 Every value a business person may change is read as a value in force with its version and is never written in code (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC11 The approval outcome is recorded on the treatment row as approval_level plus the final call, approver role, decided-at time and reason code, with no new table (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC12 A below-floor approval that cannot be recorded does not take effect and the caller's transaction is rolled back (new, D-RCV-60)

Scenario: AC13 The case status is rwb-case's; this story reports the stage outcome to the parent workflow and writes no case table (new, D-RCV-60)
